title: Spatial-Law Profile & Runtime Core

selection_basis.reduced_strict_order: MSLR-01 → MSLR-03 → MSLR-04 → MSLR-07 → MSLR-08 → MSLR-13 → MSLR-14 → MSLR-16 → MSLR-18

objective: Implement the reduced MSLR opening seam: reusable SpatialLawProfile and dimension-rule schemas; a distinct live SpatialLawRuntimeInstance boundary; explicit intrinsic-law/geometry vs substrate/discretization vs projection separation; finite/quotient/unbounded/procedurally-addressed extent semantics; scope/invariant/composition/precedence validation; stable owner identity independent of coordinates; owner-reference/version compatibility bindings; a baseline normal/Euclidean profile; projection-invariance guarantees; and migration/version hooks without creating duplicate World, Reality, Scene, Map, Environment, Action/Event, Transition, Portal, Visibility, or Knowledge ledgers.
acceptance: Reusable profile definition and live runtime instance remain distinct and versioned.
Default Euclidean profile validates with no anomalous law state.
Intrinsic spatial law/geometry, optional runtime substrate/discretization and projection/presentation are explicit distinct layers.
Topology, metric, containment/scale and orientation rules remain distinct dimensions and compose only through explicit profile semantics.
Projection changes alone do not change canonical identity, intrinsic distance, adjacency, containment, orientation or accepted law state.
Canonical owner identity is independent of screen, floating projection, tiling-cell or runtime coordinate representation.
Profiles can declare finite, quotient, unbounded or procedurally-addressed/lazy extent semantics without requiring exhaustive enumeration.
Contradictory rules without explicit precedence/resolution fail deterministically.
Unsupported dimension/property remains unresolved rather than inferred.
Owner-backed World/Reality/Scene/Transition/Portal/Visibility/Knowledge references retain canonical identity and version authority; MSLR creates no duplicate spatial ledger.
Compatibility/version checks fail closed on missing, stale or incompatible owner references.
Migration/version hooks transform profile schema representations only and do not silently mutate canonical runtime/owner state.
Blocking profile/runtime workflows remain semantic/nonvisual, keyboard-capable, provider-off, optional-AI independent, and paid-cloud independent.
boundaries: MBES-24 and all upstream completed programs remain sealed.
World/Reality/Scene retain canonical place, reality and scene identity/state.
Transition/Portal owners retain traversal and portal truth.
Visibility/Knowledge owners retain authorization and participant-knowledge truth.
GPR/Action/Event retain generic execution, Event history and replay authority.
MCS remains map/cartographic projection authority; a map is never spatial truth.
MSLR-01 creates no second World, Reality, Scene, Map, Environment, Action/Event, Transition, Portal, Visibility or Knowledge ledger.
MSLR-03 and later MSLR tranches remain unauthorized until canonical MSLR-01 closeout.
MSLR projection coordinates and substrate addresses are derived bindings only and never replace canonical owner identity.
Regular hyperbolic {p,q} tiling mathematics is optional specialized authoring/generator validation and is not a universal MSLR formula.
External hyperbolic/HyperRogue research informs clean-room generalized architecture only; no protected implementation, assets, maps, UI expression or save formats are copied.
